oneTimers: Restructuring and other charges were a $30M net credit this quarter — a benefit from reducing the previously accrued European Commission fine recorded in 2023 — versus a $57M charge a year ago. For the full year, restructuring and other charges were $2,191M, mostly severance and asset impairments under the 2025 Restructuring Plan.

A $109M mark-to-market loss on Escrowed Shares — Intel shares held in escrow for the U.S. Department of Commerce under the CHIPS Act Secure Enclave agreement — sits inside interest and other, net; Intel excludes it from non-GAAP results. The full-year mark-to-market loss was $1,796M.
Gains (losses) on equity investments, net were a $97M loss, mostly mark-to-market and price adjustments on Intel's investment portfolio rather than chip sales; also excluded from non-GAAP results.
otherDetail: Other income of $(242)M combines a $97M loss on equity investments, net with $145M of interest and other, net. The $671M tax provision on $338M of pre-tax income is a 198.5% effective rate — the tax bill alone exceeds pre-tax profit, which is why a $580M operating profit became a net loss.

segments.name: Client Computing Group
segments.note: PC and client chips; down 7% YoY as the PC market softened. Segment operating income was $2,209M, down from $3,194M a year ago.

segments.name: Data Center and AI
segments.note: Xeon server chips and AI data-center products; up 9% YoY. Segment operating income was $1,250M, up from $374M a year ago.

segments.name: Intel Foundry
segments.note: Intel's chip factories, shown at their $222M of sales to OUTSIDE customers only. Foundry's total segment revenue was $4,507M, but $4,285M of that was wafers sold to Intel's own product groups — counting it here would count the same dollars twice. Foundry lost $2,509M in the quarter.

segments.name: All other
segments.note: Mobileye (self-driving tech) and smaller businesses, after Altera was deconsolidated in September 2025. Intel reports this group at $574M; it is shown as $522M here, net of $52M of intersegment eliminations not attributable to Foundry, so the parts sum exactly to Intel's $13,674M total. Down 48% YoY largely because Altera's sales left the group.

takeaways.text: Intel earned $580M from operations on $13,674M of revenue, but a $671M tax provision — a 198.5% rate on $338M of pre-tax income — turned that into a $333M net loss, and $591M attributable to Intel after $258M went to non-controlling interests. On a non-GAAP basis at a 12% tax rate, Intel earned $767M, or $0.15 a share.
takeaways.title: A tax bill bigger than the profit

takeaways.text: Data Center and AI revenue rose 9% to $4,737M with $1,250M of segment operating income, up from $374M a year ago. Client Computing fell 7% to $8,193M, though it still earned $2,209M — the PC business remains Intel's profit engine while servers provide the growth.
takeaways.title: Data centers grew while PCs shrank

takeaways.text: Intel Foundry booked $4,507M of revenue but lost $2,509M. Only $222M came from outside customers (10-K: $307M for the full year less $85M in the first nine months). The rest is Intel charging itself, which is why $4,337M of intersegment sales is eliminated again in consolidation.
takeaways.title: Foundry still loses money — and mostly sells to Intel

verdict: Intel's revenue fell 4% to $13.7B and it lost $333M, as a $671M tax bill — almost double its pre-tax profit — wiped out a modest operating profit, even though data-center sales grew 9%.
